message: DMARC policy is p=none, which is monitoring only: receivers report on spoofed mail but still deliver it. That protects the domain no more than having no DMARC record.
suggestion: Use the aggregate reports to confirm every legitimate sender passes SPF or DKIM alignment, then raise p= to quarantine and, once stable, to reject.

message: DMARC record has no rua= tag, so you will not receive aggregate reports.
SPF on example.com uses ~all (softfail). Receivers typically accept the mail and only mark it; -all is stronger and expected with an enforced DMARC policy.
suggestion: Switch ~all to -all once every legitimate sending service is listed in the SPF record.

message: No MTA-STS TXT record at _mta-sts.example.com. Receivers will not require STARTTLS to a pinned MX set.
suggestion: Publish `_mta-sts.example.com` TXT `v=STSv1; id=<unique>` and a policy at https://mta-sts.example.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt.

message: No TLS-RPT record at _smtp._tls.example.com. You will not receive SMTP TLS failure reports.
DKIM can't be assessed yet: no signing selectors for example.com have been seen in aggregate reports.
suggestion: Add a selector to check it now, or wait for aggregate reports to show which selectors your senders sign with.

message: No BIMI record at default._bimi.example.com. Inbox logo branding is not advertised.
suggestion: BIMI requires DMARC p=quarantine/reject at pct=100 plus a TXT at default._bimi.example.com: `v=BIMI1; l=https://...svg`.
